known_gaps.description: SESSION-TIMING ERROR (user-caught 2026-07-18, post-publish): the orchestrator treated overseas home-listing/local-index moves (Taiwan exchange -7.29% for TSM's 2330.TW listing, KOSPI -6.37% for EWY's underlying, ASML.AS -3.84%, STMPA.PA -3.91%) as leading indicators implying a 'pending Monday gap' on the corresponding US-listed securities. This is backwards: Asian exchanges (Taiwan, Korea) and European exchanges (Amsterdam, Paris) close well before the US session opens on the same calendar day, so any Friday move in those markets is ALREADY available information by the time the US session trades -- the US close (verified via direct yfinance quotes: TSM -2.77%, EWY -0.50%, ASML -2.09%, STM -1.13%) is the fully-priced reaction, not a preview of something still to come. The correct framing: cross-listed securities and country ETFs often show markedly DAMPENED reactions vs their home market/index (differing investor base, index/circuit-breaker effects, local-vs-global fundamental weighting) -- that dampening is itself worth noting, but never as 'pending' risk. NEVER again frame a same-day overseas session move as a future US-session risk; always pull the US ticker's own live quote directly (get_stock_price) before making any gap/timing claim, rather than inferring it from a foreign listing.
